transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (SummitPay Head of ML), Ben Hart (SummitPay Infra Eng), Priya Singh (SummitPay Product)
Artifacts shared: Redwood Optimize deck (link), cost model spreadsheet (https://redwood.app/link/cost-models/summitpay), benchmark baseline CSV

Summary: quick walkthrough of Redwood Optimize recommendations focused on batching and prefix/KV cache setup; high level cost model for SummitPay's chat/transaction enrichment workload; agreed next steps: send tailored cost model, run short benchmark, schedule security deep dive.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): hey everyone, thanks for joining, should be about 45-ish minutes, we built a short deck and then arjun will demo the optimize console and a cost model for your workload
00:22 Speaker 2 (Lena): yep, thanks Maya, appreciate it, we really just want to understand how much we can save on per-token cost and keep latency under 300ms p95 for interactive flows
00:36 Speaker 1 (Maya): totally, that's our goal — arjun, do you want to take it away on batching and KV cache?
00:40 Speaker 3 (Arjun): sure, thanks Maya, hi Lena, Ben, Priya, quick background — SummitPay sample is mostly short chat turns plus a few longer transaction context calls, so two main levers: batching (to amortize kernel overhead) and prefix/KV cache (to avoid recomputing expensive prefixes). we'll show the console recommendations and a cost model.
01:15 Speaker 3 (Arjun): quick note on terms, i might say "kv cash" by mistake in the demo, when i mean KV cache, also "prefix cache" is the same idea for repeated context.
01:28 Speaker 2 (Ben): and we are on AWS EKS today with a mix of burst nodes, latency concern is mostly during peak auth flows
01:40 Speaker 3 (Arjun): got it — two immediate architecture options: hosted (Redwood API) for fastest time to value, or Dedicated/Private for pinned capacity and VPC. both support KV cache — for Private we can integrate with your KMS and VPC peers.
02:05 Speaker 1 (Maya): we'll show a cost example with hosted assumptions and a separate column for dedicated amortized costs.
02:33 Speaker 3 (Arjun): demoing console now — Optimize tab, the recommendations engine ingests your traffic profile (we used the traces you provided) and suggests batch sizes and caching TTLs. for SummitPay sample we suggested batching window = 12–20ms for throughput, with a micro-batching fallback to keep p95 low.
03:10 Speaker 3 (Arjun): transcript note: when i say "micro batching" i mean small aggregation per GPU tick; sometimes that interacts weirdly with your network queuing if you have uneven request sizes.
03:42 Speaker 4 (Priya): are there recommendations for prioritizing auth vs enrichment flows? the enrichment has higher token counts.
03:52 Speaker 3 (Arjun): yes, you can set routing policies per route — keep auth on a low-latency route (no batching or tiny batch) and enrichment on batched capacity; Optimize will auto-suggest split percentages.
04:20 Speaker 2 (Lena): can you explain the prefix vs KV cache again?
04:30 Speaker 3 (Arjun): sure — prefix cache stores decoded prefix tokens (or KV cache entries) so when a request repeats earlier context we reuse the KV cache on the GPU and skip recomputing transformer layers. it saves tokens and latency for repeated prompts. prefix cache is most effective when a high fraction of requests share beginning context, like templates or system prompts.
05:12 Speaker 3 (Arjun): for SummitPay we saw about 18% repeat prefix across the sample. that translates into a steady-state token reduction.
05:28 Speaker 2 (Ben): ok how much memory does the KV cache need per session? we need to know GPU memory footprint to size pods.
05:38 Speaker 3 (Arjun): rough ballpark: depends on model and sequence length; e.g., for a 70B model with 2k context, a typical KV cache per active session is ~6–10MB. with quantized kernels numbers shift slightly. we'll add a sizing table in the follow-up.
06:05 Speaker 4 (Priya): any impact on cold-starts? like if a user hasn't hit the cached prefix, do we see a big latency spike?
06:15 Speaker 3 (Arjun): cold-starts look like uncached hits — you get full per-token decode time the first time, but Optimize suggests warmup strategies and async prefetch for top templates to reduce that.
06:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): switching to the cost model slide — arjun, walk us through the assumptions you used for SummitPay.
06:55 Speaker 3 (Arjun): assumptions: 1) model family = redwood-13B equivalent for baseline, 2) average tokens per enrichment request = 420 tokens, average auth request = 48 tokens, 3) traffic mix = 70% auth (low token) / 30% enrichment (high token), 4) traffic shape from 9am-11am peak and evenings we modeled.
07:25 Speaker 2 (Lena): we actually expect more enrichment during peak, maybe closer to 40/60.
07:32 Speaker 3 (Arjun): noted — that will push throughput and cost up; in the spreadsheet we left those as editable knobs.
07:44 Speaker 3 (Arjun): example numbers: hosted baseline without caching/batching = $X per 1M requests (spreadsheet has exact), with batching tuned we see ~22% CPU/GPU efficiency improvement, with KV cache at observed 18% repeat we factor another 15% token reduction, combined end-to-end cost delta ~32% in this scenario.
08:20 Speaker 2 (Ben): is that 32% per-token cost or overall infra spend including networking?
08:28 Speaker 3 (Arjun): that's per-token compute spend — we include an estimated networking + infra overhead in a separate column, typically adds 5–10% depending on region.
08:45 Speaker 4 (Priya): how do you model latency increases from batching? we can't let auth exceed 300ms p95.
08:55 Speaker 3 (Arjun): Optimize enforces latency SLOs as hard constraints during recommendation generation; for auth routes we set a p95 constraint of 300ms and the engine recommends batch size=1–3 and immediate dispatch; enrichment route can tolerate larger micro-batching.
09:22 Speaker 1 (Maya): security questions? Ben had a note about VPC and KMS.
09:30 Speaker 2 (Ben): yes, for Private we need KMS integration for key wrapping, and audit logs forwarded to our splunk. also SOC2 evidence.
09:42 Speaker 3 (Arjun): Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit log exports; we'll include a checklist in follow-up. SOC2 and ISO attestation docs link will be in the packet.
10:05 Speaker 2 (Lena): any concerns about cache poisoning or stale KV entries?
10:12 Speaker 3 (Arjun): good question — we include cache TTLs and validation rules; Optimize can recommend conservative TTLs for sensitive routes and provide invalidation hooks. we also recommend request-level cache keys that include request-specific nonces when needed.
10:45 Speaker 4 (Priya): what about dedup across sessions, do you dedup on hashed prompts?
10:52 Speaker 3 (Arjun): we support dedup semantics: you can hash prefix+user-profile to increase reuse but watch for privacy. for SummitPay's privacy constraints we recommended per-customer hashing (not global).
11:20 Speaker 3 (Arjun): switching back to the console — here's a sample benchmark we ran: baseline throughput 600 tokens/sec per A100-like instance, with batched pipelines we hit 820 tokens/sec; with prefix cache we reduced effective tokens by 15% on sample set.
12:05 Speaker 2 (Ben): can you run that same bench on our sample traces?
12:09 Speaker 3 (Arjun): yes that's in the next steps — arjun will run a 48-72 hr local benchmark using SummitPay traces and a 13B equivalent model.
12:20 Speaker 2 (Lena): what's the expected infra commit if we go Dedicated? like number of GPUs?
12:28 Speaker 3 (Arjun): depends on traffic mix; ballpark for peak you might need 6–8 SXM GPUs for steady 95th throughput at current projections; Optimize shows a recommended dedicated pool sizing page we can share.
13:05 Speaker 2 (Ben): give me the quick tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for our case.
13:10 Speaker 1 (Maya): hosted = fastest onboarding, usage-based, easy to iterate; dedicated = reserved capacity with better predictability and lower unit costs at scale; private = full control, VPC/KMS and audit for compliance but more ops. you can start hosted and then migrate to dedicated or private as you commit.
13:45 Speaker 4 (Priya): about model variants — do you fallback if capacity constrained?
13:52 Speaker 3 (Arjun): yes, smart routing can fallback to lower-cost model variant for non-critical routes to keep SLAs. Optimize can simulate fallback cost/latency too.
14:10 Speaker 2 (Lena): any hard numbers on percent savings when you use both batching + KV cache on a mixed workload?
14:18 Speaker 3 (Arjun): in our spreadsheet we show scenarios — conservative combined savings 18–25%, typical 25–35%, optimistic 35–45% depending on repeat rate and batch efficiency.
14:45 Speaker 2 (Ben): curious about implementation effort — how long to integrate KV cache with our stack?
14:51 Speaker 3 (Arjun): for hosted it's just config + route keys; for Private/Dedicated you'll deploy a lightweight Redis for cache metadata or rely on in-memory per-GPU caching. typical integration 2–4 weeks for dev + staging tests.
15:25 Speaker 4 (Priya): do you have guidance for TTLs and eviction?
15:32 Speaker 3 (Arjun): yes — default TTL for ephemeral auth contexts we suggest 5–30s, for templates maybe 5–10 minutes, but depends on churn. Optimize will recommend TTLs based on measured repeat windows.
16:00 Speaker 2 (Lena): can Optimize simulate quality degradation if we quantize models to save cost?
16:08 Speaker 3 (Arjun): yes, we test recommended quantization profiles and generate eval diffs on held-out prompts; if quality drops beyond your threshold we flag it. we'll include eval runs in the benchmark.
16:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): interruption — quick question from Priya, are there any legal/reg constraints for storing cached user data?
16:48 Speaker 3 (Arjun): depends on your policy; we recommend hashing and tokenization controls; Redwood Private ensures cache stays in-customer VPC if needed.
17:10 Speaker 4 (Priya): ok, for product we need to see a simple flow that shows latency impact for auth when we enable batching globally vs per-route.
17:20 Speaker 3 (Arjun): agree, we'll produce a two-column bench and a short dashboard screenshot.
17:45 Speaker 2 (Ben): network overhead for caching — do you pay extra egress on repeated hits?
17:52 Speaker 3 (Arjun): prefix/KV cache reduces compute and tokens — network impact is minimal because cache lives on the inference nodes; if you centralize cache externally there is some network cost. we'll note that in the model.
18:15 Speaker 1 (Maya): let's talk about the pilot proposal — small dedicated pool for enrichment and hosted for auth?
18:25 Speaker 3 (Arjun): that hybrid is common — dedicated GPU pool for enrichment (higher throughput, batched), hosted low-latency route for auth. Optimize shows cost and fallback configs.
18:50 Speaker 2 (Lena): timeline — we want pilot within 3 weeks if possible.
18:57 Speaker 1 (Maya): doable — next steps captured.
19:12 Speaker 3 (Arjun): demo wrap — i'll drop into the channel a runbook: config knobs (batch window, batch max size, cache TTLs, cache key strategy), plus the cost spreadsheet link.
19:40 Speaker 4 (Priya): any regressions monitoring for quality? we need evals anchored to production prompts.
19:48 Speaker 3 (Arjun): yes, Redwood Optimize integrates eval sets and monitors for quality regressions; we can wire your SLOs to alert on drift.
20:10 Speaker 2 (Ben): can we get a copy of SOC2 and the architecture whitepaper?
20:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes will include in follow-up packet.
20:35 Speaker 2 (Lena): on the cost sheet, can you show us a sensitivity analysis for percent repeat?
20:42 Speaker 3 (Arjun): yes, spreadsheet has a slider for repeat% and batch efficiency; we'll adjust to 40% enrichment as you said earlier.
21:05 Speaker 4 (Priya): about KV cache invalidation — is there an API call to evict entries per user?
21:12 Speaker 3 (Arjun): yes, eviction APIs exist; we also have TTLs and tag-based invalidation.
21:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): okay we're at about 30 minutes in, any final deep technical questions?
22:00 Speaker 2 (Ben): just one — model parallelism interplay with KV cache, do you lock sessions to GPUs?
22:10 Speaker 3 (Arjun): we do session affinity when KV cache is used heavily to avoid cross-GPU shuffles; Optimize can recommend session placement policies.
22:45 Speaker 2 (Lena): and if we need to scale out quickly for a sale event, what's the burst model?
22:52 Speaker 3 (Arjun): we support burst capacity pools and autoscaling policies; for Dedicated you can reserve burst credits.
23:10 Speaker 4 (Priya): will you include notes about per-route SLO configurations?
23:15 Speaker 3 (Arjun): yes, per-route SLO and routing policies are in the runbook.
23:45 Speaker 1 (Maya): recap — Maya to send tailored cost model and pricing, arjun to run a 48-72 hr benchmark using SummitPay traces, schedule security review, and SummitPay to provide traffic traces and VPC/KMS details.
24:05 Speaker 2 (Lena): thanks — this was helpful, we'll sync internally and get those artifacts over.
24:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): perfect, we'll follow up in the channel.

(Transcript continues with short Q&A and small clarifications; filler and occasional transcription artifacts omitted for brevity)

End of transcript.
